title: Successor placement invariant
statement: Let $n$, $src$, $dst$, $key$, $stride$, $off$, $nb$, and $cnt$ be natural numbers, and let $it,kf:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ and $\mu,\mu':\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{Z}$. Let the resource limits be $word\in\mathbb{Z}$ and $space,depth\in\mathbb{N}$. Assume $space\le word$; the source, destination, and counter intervals, of lengths $n,n,nb+1$ respectively, fit within $space$ and are pairwise apart; and for every $r<n$, the source cell at $src+r$ contains $it(r)$, the key cell at $key+it(r)\cdot stride+off$ lies within $space$ and outside both the destination and counter intervals, and contains $kf(r)<nb$. Assume also that $i<n$ and that, for every $t<nb$, the cell at $cnt+t$ in $\mu'$ contains the number of indices $r<n$ with $kf(r)<t$ plus the number of indices $r<i$ with $kf(r)=t$, while for every $j<i$, the cell at $dst+p(j)$ contains $it(j)$, where $p(j)$ is the number of indices $r<n$ with $kf(r)<kf(j)$ plus the number of indices $r<j$ with $kf(r)=kf(j)$. Form a new memory map by first setting the cell at $dst+p(i)$ to $it(i)$ and then setting the cell at $cnt+kf(i)$ to $p(i)+1$. In the resulting map, for every $t<nb$ the cell at $cnt+t$ contains the number of indices $r<n$ with $kf(r)<t$ plus the number of indices $r<i+1$ with $kf(r)=t$, and for every $j<i+1$ the cell at $dst+p(j)$ contains $it(j)$.
hypotheses_covered: Source, destination, and counter intervals fit within $space$
Source, destination, and counter intervals are pairwise apart
Each source cell contains its specified item
Each item's key cell lies within space and outside the destination and counter intervals
Each key cell contains the specified key, which is below $nb$
The counter cells contain the counts prescribed at stage $i$
The destination cells contain the specified items at their stable sorting positions for all $j<i$
